after.text:
Let E and S be types. E has a normed additive commutative group structure, a real inner product space structure, is complete and finite dimensional over the reals, and has a measurable space structure equal to its Borel structure; S has an arbitrary measurable space structure. Let V:E→R and κ∈R. Assume κ≥1, V is twice continuously Frechet differentiable over R, and for every x,v∈E the real Hessian quadratic form satisfies κ^{-1}||v||^2 ≤ D(DV)(x)[v][v] ≤ ||v||^2. Let eta:S→R and y:S→E be measurable, and assume eta(s)>0 for every s∈S. Define F(s,x)=V(x)+(eta(s)^{-1}/2)||x-y(s)||^2 for all s∈S and x∈E.
There exists one function p:S→E such that p is measurable and all the following hold simultaneously. For every s∈S, p(s)+eta(s)∇V(p(s))=y(s). For every s∈S and z∈E, F(s,p(s))+((κ^{-1}+eta(s)^{-1})/2)||z-p(s)||^2 ≤ F(s,z), and F(s,z)≤F(s,p(s)) if and only if z=p(s). For every s,t∈S, if eta(s)=eta(t), then ||p(s)-p(t)||≤||y(s)-y(t)||. Define G:S×E→E by G(s,z)=∇V(p(s)+sqrt(eta(s)) z), with multiplication of a real and a vector interpreted as scalar multiplication. This G is measurable on the product measurable space. For every s,t∈S and z,w∈E, if eta(s)=eta(t), then ||G(s,z)-G(t,w)||≤||y(s)-y(t)||+sqrt(eta(s))||z-w||. There exists a measurable measure-valued kernel K from S to E such that every K(s) is a probability measure and, for every s∈S, K(s) is exactly the pushforward of the canonical centered covariance-identity Gaussian measure on E under z↦G(s,z).
All points, directions and noise variables range over the full carrier E. The gradient is the Riesz representative of the actual Frechet derivative. The same p determines F's minimizers, G, and K. Equal eta values are hypotheses only of the two pairwise Lipschitz statements. No restriction eta≤1 occurs. E may have dimension zero, and S need not have topology, a measure, or be nonempty. K is the Gaussian gradient-output law specified above; no posterior conditional Gibbs law or HMC transition is asserted.

Define mu=volume.tilted(x↦-V(x)), R(s)=mu.tilted(x↦-||x-y(s)||^2/(2 eta(s))), and r(s) as the pushforward of R(s) under x↦sqrt(eta(s))^{-1}(x-p(s)), where real-vector multiplication is scalar multiplication. For a measure nu and real function f, nu.tilted(f) literally means nu.withDensity(x↦ENNReal.ofReal(exp(f(x))/(∫exp(f)dnu))); the real Bochner normalization is totalized if integrability fails.
The measure mu is a probability measure. Moreover, for every s∈S, all the following hold simultaneously: R(s) is a probability measure; rho(s,·) and Q(s,·) are twice continuously Frechet differentiable over R; ∇rho(s,·)(0)=0 and ∇Q(s,·)(0)=0; for every u,v∈E, 0≤D(D(rho(s,·)))(u)[v][v]≤eta(s)||v||^2; for every u,v∈E, ||v||^2≤D(D(Q(s,·)))(u)[v][v]≤(1+eta(s))||v||^2; r(s)=volume.tilted(u↦-Q(s,u)); r(s) is a probability measure; the identity map on E belongs to L2(r(s)); u↦||u||^2 is integrable with respect to r(s); ∫||u||^2 dr(s)≤dim_R(E); the function u↦∇rho(s,·)(u) belongs to L2(r(s)); ∫||∇rho(s,·)(u)||^2 dr(s)≤eta(s)^2∫||u||^2 dr(s); and ∫||∇rho(s,·)(u)||^2 dr(s)≤eta(s)^2 dim_R(E).
Here volume is the finite real Hilbert Lebesgue/Haar measure, dim_R(E) is the actual real finite dimension interpreted as a real number in the inequalities, and all Hessians and gradients are actual Frechet/Riesz objects. R(s) is the literal conditional Gibbs tilt and r(s) its centered and sqrt(eta(s))-standardized law. Equality to a tilted measure is accompanied by separate probability assertions; it is not itself interpreted as establishing probability.

For every arbitrary function F:E→R and every point p∈E, and for every real scalar s with s≠0, the pushforward under A(x)=p+s x of volume.tilted(x↦-F(x)) equals volume.tilted(x↦-F(s^{-1}(x-p))):
A_*(volume.tilted(-F)) = volume.tilted(x↦-F(s^{-1}(x-p))).
Real-vector multiplication is scalar multiplication; volume is the finite real Hilbert Lebesgue/Haar measure. For any measure nu and real function f, nu.tilted(f) literally denotes nu.withDensity(x↦ENNReal.ofReal(exp(f(x))/(∫exp(f)dnu))). This Bochner integral normalization is totalized when exponential integrability fails; the equality is equality of those literal measures. The affine map is the genuine measurable pushforward map, and the right-hand potential is composed with its inverse x↦s^{-1}(x-p). There is no CompleteSpace binder, no nontriviality assumption, and no hypothesis that F is measurable, integrable, differentiable, convex, or otherwise regular. There is no probability-measure assumption or conclusion and no assertion of exponential integrability or a positive normalization. Negative s is allowed and E may have dimension zero. The nonzero scalar is the sole explicit hypothesis after F and p; its quantifier precedes the proof argument s≠0. No Gaussian, posterior family, moment bound, or gradient conclusion occurs.
